And 2 Others Counsel for Applicant :- Abhishek Tripathi Counsel for Opposite Party :- Bhupendra Pal,G.A.
Hon'ble Dr. Gautam Chowdhary,J.

1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and Sri Bhupendra Pal,
learned counsel for the informant and perused the material on record.
2.

The instant bail cancellation application has been moved on behalf of the informant for cancelling the bail granted to the accused-opposite party nos.2 and 3 vide order dated 19.09.2024 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Court No.14, District Kanpur Nagar in Case Crime No.106 of 2024 under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B I.P.C., Police Station Kotwali, District Kanpur Nagar.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Court No.14, District Kanpur Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. Learned counsel for the applicant contends that the opposite party nos. 2 and 3 were granted bail in Case Crime No. 40 of 2023 under Sections 420, 406, 506, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C., vide order dated 29.04.2024 passed by this Court in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 7821 of 2024 on their Santosh Yadav vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18482107/
1 furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned.

sentences.text: Learned counsel further argued that the opposite parties nos. 2 and 3 filed an application dated 04.05.2024 for fixing sureties and amount of the personal bond through J.P.Singh, Advocate upon which, learned Magistrate had fixed personal bond of Rs. 1 lacs and two sureties each of the same amount, however at the stage of verification of the same, it was found that the sureties, as well as police verification and also the report of tehsildar, tehsil Bilhhaur were found forged.

Thereafter, the applicant/informant moved an application before the Additional Police Commissioner, Crime Branch, Kanpur Nagar for initiating proceedings against the accused persons upon which SWAT Team was directed to enquire into the matter and during the course of enquiry it was revealed that the surety namely, Parashuram and Vikas have stated that they do not know the accused persons and the khatauni submitted as surety is forged, on account of which, the SWAT Team recommended for registration of the F.I.R. against the accused persons.

Pursuant to which, a first information report was lodged against the accused-opposite party nos. 2, 3 and others in Case Crime No. 106 of 2024 under Sections 420, 467, 471, 120-B I.P.C. Police Station Kotwali, District Kanpur Nagar.

The opposite party no.2 and 3 moved an application for grant of bail and the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Court No.14, Kanpur Nagar vide order dated 19.09.2024 granted bail to the accused-opposite party nos. 2 and 3.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Court No.14, Kanpur Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Learned counsel further argued that the opposite party nos.
2 and 3 are the master mind behind the entire forgery committed by them to be released from jail in Case Crime No. 40 of 2023 and that they are the only person beneficiary of the forgery committed,
however the Court below while granting bail in Case Crime No. 106 of 2024 did not consider the same, therefore the bail granted to the opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 in Case Crime No. 106 of 2024 is liable to be cancelled.

4. On the other hand, learned A.G.A. has submitted that though the opposite party nos. 2and 3 were enlarged on bail vide order dated 29.04.2024 in Case Crime No. 40 of 2023 and the verification of the documents and sureties were found forged on account of which F.I.R. in Case Crime No. 106 of 2024 was lodged against the opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 in which the opposite party nos. 2 and 3 were granted bail and they have committed the offence while remaining in jail, therefore the bail granted to opposite party nos. 2 and 3 are liable to be cancelled.

5. Learned counsel for the accused-opposite party nos. 2 and 3 has submitted that the accused-opposite party no.2 and 3 were in jail and they were not aware about the act committed on behalf of them, inspite of the same F.I.R. was lodged against them in Case Crime No. 106 of 2024 in which the accused-opposite party nos. 2 and 3 have been rightly granted bail, therefore the relief sought by the applicant is liable to be rejected.

6. It is the submission of the learned counsel for the applicant that the opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 have violated the conditions of bail granted to them in Case Crime No. 40 of 2023, therefore the bail granted to the accused-opposite party no.2 and 3 in Case Crime 106 of 2024 may be cancelled.
Copy of the order of Case Crime No. 40 of 2023 is at page no. 25 of the paper book.

The conditions of that bail order reads as under:-
"(i) The applicants shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat, or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them Santosh Yadav vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18482107/
2 from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

entities.text: Santosh Yadav vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ( ii) The applicants shall not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witnesses.

(iii) The applicants shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 of Cr.P.C.
(iv) The applicants shall file an undertaking to the effect that they shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in the trial court.
(v) The applicants shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed,
either personally or through their counsel.
(vi) The applicants shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail."
7. Perusal of the condition no. (vi) shows that the accused-opposite party nos. 2 and 3 shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.

In the instant case, it is evident that the accused-opposite party nos. 2 and 3 were in jail and their pairokar have filled up personal bond and sureties bond which were found to be forged on account of which they have not been released from jail and have remained incarcerated.

Separate F.I.R. has been registered in Case Crime No. 106 of 2024 for the act of forgery committed on their behalf, in which the accused-opposite party nos. 2 and 3 have been granted bail, which is sought to be cancelled.

The Court is of the opinion that though, the opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 are the beneficiary of the forgery committed on their behalf, it is on record that consequent to the forgery coming to light, the accused opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 have not been released from jail and are still under incarceration.
They cannot be held liable for the act done, although on their behalf, while they were in custody.

Learned counsel for the applicant could not point out any good ground for cancelling the bail granted to the accused opposite party No. 2 and 3, in the subsequent case crime which is a separate case and therefore the bail cancellation application is liable to be rejected.
8. Accordingly, the bail cancellation application is rejected.
